answer_2.quote: (1) CaRB(1-1) considers the number of common tokens in (gold, predicted) pair for each argument of the fact. Then a one-to-one mapping is created by greedily matching gold with one of the predicted facts on the basis of token-level F1 score. (2) CaRB is a variant of CaRB(1-1) that retains CaRB(1-1)'s similarity computation, but uses a one-to-one mapping and a multi-to-one mapping for precision and recall, respectively. (3) Gestalt replaces the token-level matching strategy of CaRB(1-1) with gestalt pattern matching.
